_notes: Rules for queues, money, the fleet, reputation and catering. Kept apart from demand.json and economy.json so balance passes on demand don't touch them. Every number is a first guess unless a note says it comes from the game. Keys starting with an underscore are notes; the loader ignores them.
_service: Workers serve with customer service skill x satisfaction / 100; the player uses their skill alone. baseSkill keeps the item's base service time, zero skill takes slowestTimeFactor times as long, and skill 100 serves at fastestSpeed times the base speed. Customers complain below complainBelowSkill and are pleased from pleasedFromSkill (a reaction hook for now). queueLimits caps each vehicle's waiting customers, within queue.maxQueue; arrivals at a full queue walk on.
_queue: Customers above the service rate wait at the window. Each one gives up after patienceMinutes, spread by up to patienceSpread either way, times rainPatience while it rains. Nobody joins a queue of maxQueue people; the visible queue needs a cap anyway. An arriving customer first walks up for walkInMinutes (whole minutes, drawn evenly between the two) and only then joins the queue, checks whether it is full and starts counting their patience. An in-game minute is a second at normal speed, so 7 to 14 matches the visible queue's people walking in from 9 to 19 m along the pavement at walking pace. The walk delays sales by those minutes but doesn't change how many a window makes.
_health: Hidden cleanliness points: the sum of the daily marks of the last memoryDays days the vehicle was open. An open day without cleaning adds uncleanedDayPoints, selling stale stock adds staleStockPoints; food is stale once it has been on board staleAfterDays days (the game's food never spoils, so the mod counts from the day it first sees an item on board until that item runs out). The grade changes only when an inspector comes, about every inspectionWeeks for the current grade, with no visits inside minimumGapDays. After that each open day has chance 1 / max(1, inspectionWeeks x daysPerWeek - minimumGapDays); an ungraded vehicle uses firstInspectionWeeks. Bands from the design, which follows NYC's 0-13 / 14-27 / 28+.
_regulars: Opening at the same spot on the same weekday builds a bonus for the whole fleet: gainPerVisit per visit of at least minOpenMinutes, up to maxBonus (six weeks to +30%). Each missed week takes missPenalty off that spot and weekday.
_competition: Between the player's own vehicles only. Each other vehicle within nearbyMetres adds footfallPerNeighbour to the spot's footfall, up to maxFootfallBonus; vehicles selling the same item split that item's customers.
_fleet: The vendor licence lasts licenceDays and can be renewed in its last renewWindowDays; the City of New York sells it by phone for licenceFee dollars, and a permit for each cart or truck for permitFee. Both fees are tax-deductible and placeholders until the balance pass. There is no cap on the number of permits. travel is the game's own timing [code, unverified in game]: a taxi takes 0.04 game minutes per straight-line metre, and a cart moves at the 1.2 m/s walking pace, so a hire pushing a cart covers about 72 m per game hour at normal speed. A vehicle within stopRadiusMetres of a stop is at it; further away, the hire moves it there first. How many work a window at once is the vehicle's staff in economy.json. course is the Food Safety course the licence needs: the game has the course's name but no door for it, so the mod offers it at the business school's Market Demands door for hours hours at pricePerHour whole dollars an hour, with no course needed before it.
_catering: Gig offers arrive by text message from a bookings contact; only vehicleTypes cater. A mature fleet (maturityServed items sold) gets offersPerDayAtMaturity offers a day on average, scaled by the booking reputation, at most maxOffersPerDay. Each gig is leadDays ahead and must be accepted within replyDays. The vehicle must arrive by the start plus graceMinutes with the required category on the menu and guests x unitsPerGuest units of it, and stay to the end. The fee is guests x unitsPerGuest x the category's reference price x feeMarkup, paid on completion. A failed gig takes reputation.failure off the booking reputation, a completed one adds reputation.success. Every number is a guess.
_liveCrowds: How much of its usual crowd a venue near a pitch brings this hour (design: Live crowds from game businesses). A closed nightclub, theatre or cinema brings closedWeight. Theatre audiences come out at letOuts (minutes after midnight; 1350 is 22:30), plus weekendLetOuts at weekends (the matinee at 17:00), cinema audiences every `every` minutes from `first` to `last` (1470 is 00:30 after midnight); each surge lasts surgeMinutes at `surge` times the crowd, times weekendSurge on Saturdays and Sundays. A nightclub's guests come out for clubClosing.minutes after it closes. Offices and factories bring their staff at work divided by workers.reference, between workers.min and workers.max. The player's own nightclubs, theatres and cinemas bring their guests in the last hour divided by guests.reference, between guests.min and guests.max, times any surge; AI venues have no counts and bring their usual crowd. kinds maps the game's business types to these venues; everything else is as the area tables say. Every number is a guess.
